official.deadline_note: Applications are accepted only between 1 June and the stated application deadline, and the portal for this programme is visible only while the window is open. Up to seven months pass between submission and the committee's decision, and funding normally begins on 1 October of the following year.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 round: applications 1 June - 15 October 2026, selection during 2027, funding usually from October 2027
official.status_note: Current round is open until 15 October 2026; the DAAD Office Amman reminded applicants on 8 October 2026 that the Performing Arts scholarship deadline is 15 October 2026 and that 'days are running'.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The DAAD does not cover tuition fees: 'Please note that the DAAD does not cover tuition fees.'
benefits: Travel allowance (upon application only) and a one-off study allowance
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Under certain circumstances: monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying members of family
On application, a subsidy for justified additional costs in the case of disability or chronic illness; Green Mobility Top Up or reimbursement of carbon offset payments for air travel

German language support: course fees for an online language course, a 2-, 4- or 6-month language course before the study visit if necessary, an allowance for a personally chosen course, and reimbursement of the TestDaF or DSH test fee
eligibility: First university degree in the field of the arts, gained at the latest by the time the scholarship-supported study programme begins
University degree normally not older than 6 years at the application deadline
Full-time and attendance-based study; extra-occupational, part-time or predominantly e-learning programmes cannot be funded
Applicant must not have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline
Applicant status and country must be selectable in the DAAD portal
requirements: Applications possible only between 1 June and the stated application deadline; the DAAD portal closes at 24:00 (CET/CEST) on the last application day
Late or incomplete applications cannot be considered
All application documents in German or English; documents in other languages must be submitted with translations
Proof of current proficiency in the language of instruction of the chosen study programme; language certificates may not be older than three years
Two-step submission: documents via the DAAD portal, then work samples plus the supplementary list via the DAAD media database after the formal check
documents: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form
Letter of motivation (1-3 pages) with academic and personal reasons for the planned study project in Germany
Form 'Information about your preferred master programmes'
Current Transcript of Records with individual grades and all university degree certificates indicating final grades
Letter of acceptance from the host university if available (must be handed in before funding begins); for complementary studies: confirmation of supervision or proof that credits will be recognised
Work samples and the supplementary list, uploaded to the DAAD media database after the formal check
selection_criteria: Artistic qualification and artistic maturity, measured against study achievements and work samples
Quality of the project, measured against the study plan and the letter of motivation
The committee also gives due consideration to equal-opportunity aspects indicated in the application form
coverage: Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Possible additions: rent subsidy, family accompanying allowance, disability/chronic-illness subsidy, Green Mobility Top Up
application_method: Register in the DAAD portal (a desktop computer is required)
Complete the online application and upload the documents as PDFs in the 'Attachments' section
After the formal check, upload the work samples and the supplementary list to the DAAD media database using the emailed link
official.application_route: Online via the DAAD portal: register, complete the application form, upload PDF documents; work samples go separately to the DAAD media database only after the formal check.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants from all countries selectable in the DAAD portal, provided they have not been resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is aimed at international applicants and is funded by the Federal Foreign Office
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Only artistic projects in the Performing Arts (Drama, Theatre Directing/Theatre Dramaturgy, Musicals, Performance Studies, Dance, Choreography); applicants from Theatre and Dance Studies or with a scientific project must use other DAAD programmes
official.duration: 10 to 24 months for a Master's/postgraduate degree course; one academic year (usually 12 months) for complementary studies without degree
official.description: DAAD's own framing: the programme offers the opportunity to continue your education in Germany with a postgraduate or continuing course of study and also promotes the exchange of experience and networking amongst colleagues. It funds either a Master's/postgraduate degree course at a state or state-recognised German university or a complementary course without degree, and is funded by the Federal Foreign Office.
official.program_type: Master's degree/postgraduate degree course or complementary studies without degree
official.english_requirement: Proof of current proficiency in the language of instruction of the chosen study programme (German, English or both), held at the latest by the start of the scholarship; language certificates may not be older than three years, and an application must show how the required level will be reached if it is not yet held

not_confirmed: Selection date for the current cycle (the announcement states only that up to seven months can pass between submission and notification)
Exact travel allowance amount (published only as 'travel allowance upon application only')
Whether the next cycle's window will again open on 1 June (the announcement states deadlines are updated at least once a year and are usually in the same period as the previous year)
verification.notes: Amount, benefits, eligibility and procedure taken from the DAAD scholarship database entry (updated 11 October 2026); work-sample formats from the DAAD performing-arts information page; the 15 October 2026 deadline confirmed by the DAAD Office Amman announcement of 8 October 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: This DAAD scholarship pays a flat EUR 992 per month plus a travel allowance and a one-off study allowance for a full-time Master's or a one-year complementary project in drama, theatre directing/dramaturgy, musicals, performance studies, dance or choreography at a German state or state-recognised university. It explicitly does not pay tuition, so any university fees are on you. Applications run only from 1 June to 15 October through the DAAD portal, with your artistic work samples uploaded separately to the DAAD media database after the formal check, and funding would normally start on 1 October 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Practising performing artists holding a first arts degree earned within roughly the last six years who want a German arts-university Master's or a supervised complementary year in Germany.
application_readiness_checklist: Register early on the DAAD portal using a desktop computer, and prepare PDFs of your CV, a 1-3 page motivation letter, and transcripts/degree certificates with German or English translations
Complete the 'Information about your preferred master programmes' form even if you have only one university of choice or already hold an admission letter

Cut work samples to the exact per-discipline rules on the DAAD performing-arts page (e.g. about 3 minutes self-introduction plus two 5-10 minute role excerpts for drama) and name files DAADreference_Last_First_Field_Title
Check that your language certificate is less than three years old, or show in the application how you will reach the required level before funding starts
common_rejection_risks: Uploading work samples to the DAAD portal instead of the DAAD media database, or submitting a format outside the permitted list (MP3, WAV, MPEG, MP4, MOV, JPEG, JPG, PNG, TIF, GIF, PDF, INDD, PSD, CR2, EPS, DOC, DOCX, XML, PPTX, PPT)
Non-artistic or theoretical projects: Theatre Studies, Dance Studies or scientific projects belong to the 'Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines' programme instead
A first degree older than six years, more than 15 months' residence in Germany, or a part-time/e-learning-heavy programme
SSupplementary list missing from the media-database upload, or assuming an admission letter can wait until after the award - it must be in hand before the funding period begins
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees (the DAAD does not cover them), entrance-examination costs, semester contributions, and any shortfall between the flat EUR 992 and actual living costs until a rent subsidy is approved.
document_audit: Only PDFs can be uploaded to the portal; translations must be uploaded together with the original-language document
Language certificates older than three years are not accepted
Complementary-studies applicants need the professor's confirmation of supervision or proof of credit recognition by the home university
The admission letter can be missing at application time but must be submitted before the funding period begins
alerts: The 15 October 2026 deadline is only days away and the portal shuts hard at 24:00 CET/CEST; applications are accepted only between 1 June and the deadline, so a miss means waiting a full year
Up to seven months can pass between submission and the committee's decision, so plan your study and job offers for late spring 2027 and an October 2027 start

A scholarship offer is not an admission: you need the host university's admission (often including an entrance examination whose dates fall months earlier and whose costs are not covered) before the funding becomes valid, and the German-language course is mandatory where the language of instruction at your host institution is German
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Two-step: written documents go through the DAAD portal first; only after the formal check do you receive a link to upload work samples and the supplementary list to the DAAD media database.

official.deadline_note: Two binding rounds a year, ending 1 March and 1 September, with the portal opening about six weeks before each deadline. The foundation has announced that from 1 March 2027 it will only accept applications for first-cycle programmes, so this round is the last one open to Master's applicants; non-EU nationals may in addition apply only at irregular intervals.
official.application_cycle: Spring 2027 round: portal 15 January - 1 March 2027 (the Fall 2026 round closed 1 September 2026; Fall 2027: 15 July - 1 September 2027)
official.status_note: Applications are accepted in two rounds per year; the Fall 2026 round ended on 1 September 2026 and the next window opens on 15 January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: For AA-funded students: 'reimbursement of tuition fees in Germany of up to 10,000 EUR per year' is listed among the optional components, and the official information sheet states that for non-EU applicants tuition funding is 'in certain cases possible in Germany'. For the EU/BMFTR track, tuition funding in Germany is not possible.
benefits: Base scholarship of 992 EUR per month for Master's students (AA-funded track); 1,500 EUR per month for PhD candidates
Health insurance allowance of up to 100 EUR per month (Master's) or up to 200 EUR per month (PhD)
Fixed fringe benefits of 38 EUR per month
Reimbursement of tuition fees in Germany of up to 10,000 EUR per year (in certain cases), and tuition fees for German language courses
Family allowance and child allowances per child (the overview sheet lists the family allowance at up to 276 EUR)
Ideational support, the foundation's event programme and its alumni network
eligibility: International students who have completed their first degree abroad can apply prior to starting a Master's degree programme in Germany
All disciplines may apply to study full-time at a state or state-recognised university in Germany; only Master's programmes with a standard duration of four semesters or more are funded
International PhD students who have completed their graduate degree abroad may apply for a PhD programme in Germany
Priority is given to applicants from DAC countries who have not yet taken up residence in Germany at the time of their application
The AA-funded track is aimed at Bildungsauslaender (not educated in Germany) from outside the EU; the BMFTR track is aimed at German nationals, Bildungsinlaender educated in Germany and EU nationals
Refugees can apply under the same conditions as all other applicants
requirements: Online application only via the foundation's portal, which is accessible at least six weeks before the deadline; the 1 March and 1 September deadlines are binding with no exceptions
Only complete applications can be processed; the enrolment certificate is the single exception and may follow until the stage-3 interview at the latest
All documents in German (personal and expert references also accepted in English, but not in any other language); certified translations where required
International applicants: written proof of German proficiency at level DSH 1 or B2, preferably with the application and at the latest by stage 3
The personal reference and the expert report must come from two different people, and references sent directly by referees must reach the foundation by the deadline
Any additional income must be offset against the scholarship payment (earnings limit for marginal employment under Section 8 (1) No. 1 SGB IV)
documents: Application form (Bewerbungsbogen Studienstipendium) with personal data and CV, motivation for applying to the foundation, subject interests and social commitments
Copy of the university entrance qualification including proof of individual grades
Certified copy of the first degree certificate with individual grades (Transcript of Records), plus an explanation of the grading if it differs from the German system
Student enrolment certificate, which may be submitted as late as the stage-3 selection interview
Written proof of German language skills (international German Abitur, or at least DSH 1 or level B2)
Third-party reference on social commitment and an expert report from a university lecturer, each on the foundation's own form
selection_criteria: Very good school or university academic record
Convincing reasons for applying to the Heinrich Boell Foundation
German language proficiency (DSH 1 or level B2)
Three-stage procedure: written application, interview with a liaison lecturer, then a digital interview with the selection committee; candidates rejected after stage 3 cannot re-apply
coverage: Base scholarship of 992 EUR per month (Master's, AA track) or 1,500 EUR per month (PhD, AA track)
Health insurance allowance of up to 100 EUR (Master's) or 200 EUR (PhD) per month
Fixed fringe benefits of 38 EUR per month
Tuition fees in Germany in certain cases, up to 10,000 EUR per year, plus German language course fees
Family allowance and child allowances per child
Not covered: periods of study abroad receive no additional funding; study-abroad funding exists only on the BMFTR track
application_method: Register in the online portal when it opens about six weeks before the deadline
Complete the application form using Adobe Acrobat Reader only and upload all documents as PDFs
Submit the application online; referees may send references directly to studienwerk@boell.de by the deadline
official.application_route: Online only via the foundation's application portal: register in the six-week window before the 1 March or 1 September deadline, complete the application form, upload all PDF documents and submit.
official.study_mode: Full-time study at a state or state-recognised university in Germany
official.citizenship_residency: AA track: applicants from outside the EU who obtained their higher education entrance qualification abroad; BMFTR track: German nationals, Bildungsinlaender educated in Germany and EU nationals. DAC-country applicants still residing abroad receive priority.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the graduate scholarship is aimed at international students (Bildungsauslaender) from outside the EU; EU nationals apply via the BMFTR track, and graduates of German schools abroad apply under the same requirements as students educated in Germany
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All disciplines qualify for the graduate and PhD scholarships; only Master's programmes with a standard duration of four semesters or more are funded
official.duration: The regular period of study of the funded programme, which may be extended by one semester
official.description: The foundation's own framing: scholarships for graduate students and PhD students from DAC countries who intend to pursue a Master's degree or PhD in Germany, implemented under the guidelines of the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) and the Federal Foreign Office (AA), with two application procedures each year.

not_confirmed: Health insurance allowance for the AA-funded PhD track: the financial support page states up to 200 EUR per month, while the October 2026 overview sheet lists the health insurance allowance under BMFTR only
Exact dates of the irregularly announced application windows for non-EU nationals (the information sheet states they may apply only at irregular intervals)
Whether the 1 March 2027 round will definitively be the last round accepting Master's applications (the foundation announces first-cycle-only applications from that date)
verification.notes: Amounts and components checked on the financial support page and the October 2026 overview sheet; deadlines on the scholarships, applying and Studienstipendium pages; documents, selection stages and German-language requirement from the February 2026 information sheet A1-1b (PDF).

applicant_utility.summary: The Heinrich Boell Foundation funds international Master's and PhD students outside the EU (DAC countries get priority) with EUR 992 per month for Master's students and EUR 1,500 for PhD candidates, plus a health-insurance allowance, possible tuition reimbursement of up to EUR 10,000 a year, and family allowances. The only route is the foundation's online portal in the windows 15 January - 1 March or 15 July - 1 September, and international applicants need German at DSH 1 or B2 level, proven by the stage-3 interview at the latest. Note the foundation's announcement that from 1 March 2027 it will only accept applications for first-cycle programmes, which makes the 1 March 2027 round the last one for Master's applicants.
applicant_utility.best_fit: DAC-country and other non-EU graduates with strong grades, documented social engagement and roughly B1-B2 German who want a Master's of at least four semesters, or a PhD, in Germany before moving there.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up two different referees early - one university lecturer for the expert report and one non-family member for the social-commitment reference - and brief them to use the foundation's own forms
Complete the application form in Adobe Acrobat Reader only and keep answers inside the printed boxes, since answers must be legible on a paper printout
Assemble certified translations and a grading explanation (Modified Bavarian Formula) for the entrance qualification and first degree, and compute your average grade yourself if it is not given
Book a DSH 1 or B2 test so the certificate can be submitted with the application rather than at stage 3, and watch for the portal opening on 15 January 2027
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete files: references that arrive by post after the deadline or by a different route than the one agreed, or the enrolment certificate still missing at the stage-3 interview
Personal reference and expert report coming from the same person, or a reference written by a friend, family member or an internship supervisor
A Master's programme with a standard duration under four semesters, or applying after the Master's programme has already begun
Answers overflowing the application form's boxes so they are cut off or illegible in print, and rejection after reaching stage 3 once already, which permanently bars a re-application
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Semester contributions and any tuition above the EUR 10,000 per year reimbursement cap, plus the gap between EUR 992 and living costs in expensive cities, with no additional funding for any study period abroad.
document_audit: Copies of degrees must be certified, and anything not in German or English except the two references needs a certified translation
The enrolment certificate is the only document allowed to follow; everything else must be complete by the deadline
References must carry the referee's contact details and signature unless the referee emails them directly from their own account
Do not wait for the last day to submit, as the portal is known to be overloaded on deadline day
alerts: The 1 March and 1 September deadlines are binding with no exceptions, and non-EU nationals may apply only at irregularly announced intervals, so check the scholarship pages before the portal opens on 15 January 2027
From 1 March 2027 the foundation will only accept applications for first-cycle programmes, so Master's applicants should treat this round as their final opportunity
Any side income is deducted from the scholarship using the marginal-employment earnings limit, so factor that into your budget planning
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in the password-protected portal about six weeks before the deadline, complete the PDF application form, upload all documents, submit, and have referees send references directly to studienwerk@boell.de by the same deadline.
